targets.old_statement: Safe eyes ride twelve seconds ahead, one block in town or four on highways, while the separate four second sight rule caps speed against visible distance.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Safe eyes ride twelve seconds ahead, one block in town or four on highways, while the separate four second sight rule caps speed against visible distance.
targets.statement: Safer drivers look at least twelve seconds ahead, about one block in city traffic or four city blocks on the highway, while the four-second sight-distance rule checks whether you are driving too fast for the distance you can clearly see.

targets.old_statement: Left turns bow to every oncoming vehicle and bike with double rechecks, whereas right turns on red need only a full stop, clear lefts and paths, and no banning sign.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Left turns bow to every oncoming vehicle and bike with double rechecks, whereas right turns on red need only a full stop, clear lefts and paths, and no banning sign.
targets.statement: Before turning left, yield to oncoming traffic including bicycles, check that the target street is clear, and look toward oncoming traffic once more; before turning right, check left and oncoming turning traffic, check for pedestrians, never turn right immediately after passing a bicycle, and on red stop first unless a sign prohibits turning.

targets.old_statement: Slow bikes may be passed inside no passing zones when sight allows, yet bike lanes themselves forbid driving, parking and stopping except crossings and emergencies.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Slow bikes may be passed inside no passing zones when sight allows, yet bike lanes themselves forbid driving, parking and stopping except crossings and emergencies.
targets.statement: You may pass a slow-moving bicyclist in a no-passing zone if you can do so safely, whereas stopping, parking, or driving in a designated bicycle path or lane is prohibited unless entering or leaving an alley or driveway, performing official duties, following a police officer's direction, or facing an emergency, while yielding to bicycles.
